To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
saturated fat increases intrahepatic fat content and insulin resistance more than unsaturated fat or simple sugars.
saturated fat intake induces the most severe hepatic steatosis, insulin resistance, inflammation and endotoxemias, and ceramide accumulation.
dietary saturated fat increases intrahepatic lipid content more than dietary unsaturated fat or dietary carbohydrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diet on liver fat and the pathways that contribute to it.

the effects of dietary macronutrients on pathways contributing to ITHG, and the metabolic and molecular mechanisms that underlie the effects of dietary composition on ITHG and its associated metabolic risk factors.
the role that diet plays in the development and progression of obesity, insulin resistance, diabetes and fatty liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a diet high in saturated fat and low in unsaturated fat is more metabolically harmful to the human liver than a diet high in unsaturated fat and low in saturated fat.
the saturated fats in our diet are more metabolically harmful to the human liver than either the unsaturated fats or simple sugars.
a high fat diet, especially one that is high in saturated fat, is more metabolically harmful to the liver than a high carbohydrate or a high unsaturated fat diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the type of fat you eat has a significant effect on your body composition.
saturated fat is more metabolically harmful than unsaturated fat or simple sugars for the human liver.
a diet high in saturated fat increases liver fat and is more harmful to the liver than a diet high in unsaturated fat or simple carbohydrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
saturated fat is more metabolically harmful than other dietary macronutrients.
saturated fat is more harmful to your liver than unsaturated fat or simple sugars.
the composition of excess calories is important in the context of liver fat.
